MRI radiomics combined with artificial intelligence (AI) has been explored for non-invasive preoperative TDs detection. However, results vary across studies; therefore, we performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to pool their diagnostic test accuracy (DTA). Methods: This systematic review and DTA meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Diagnostic Test Accuracy and reported in adherence to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses of Diagnostic Test Accuracy Studies (PRISMA-DTA). Databases were screened for DTA studies of MRI-based radiomics predicting TDs in adult RC patients with histopathology as reference. Results: Nine studies (2589 patients) were identified. Across included studies, the bivariate meta-analysis showed pooled sensitivity of 0.765 (95% CI 0.714 - 0.809) and specificity of 0.790 (95% CI 0.750 - 0.825), with overall AUC of 0.845 and very low heterogeneity (I2 = 7.3%). In validation datasets, diagnostic performance remained consistent (AUC 0.806), with pooled sensitivity 0.751 (95% CI 0.681 - 0.809) and specificity 0.751 (95% CI 0.681 - 0.809). For MRI modality, T2 weighted image (T2WI) showed higher sensitivity (0.745) than T2WI plus diffusion weighted image (DWI) (0.697), while T2WI+DWI had higher specificity (0.809 vs 0.737) and AUC (0.829 vs 0.796), with no significant subgroup differences (p[≥]0.192). Models combining radiomics with clinical/radiological variables achieved significantly higher sensitivity (0.842 vs 0.657, p<0.001) and higher AUC (0.827 vs 0.752), with comparable specificity. Conclusion: MRI-based radiomics demonstrates good accuracy for preoperative detection of tumor deposits in RC. The integration of radiomics with clinical or imaging features increases the accuracy of identification. Amongst the MRI modalities, models that utilize the combination of T2WI plus DWI are more accurate than those using T2WI or DWI only.
ncf53d2d8d2b6: Background: Homologous recombination deficiency (HRD) is an important predictive biomarker for poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitor (PARPi) therapy in ovarian cancer (OC). However, real-world data on HRD prevalence and assay performance in Indian patients are limited. This study evaluated commercial HRD assays, then developed an in-house HRD assay and characterized HRD and BRCA alterations in a large real-world Indian OC cohort. Methods: This retrospective study included 4,163 formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) OC samples tested between 2021 and 2025. HRD and BRCA status were initially assessed using the AmoyDx HRD Focus Panel (n=1,097) and SOPHiA DDM HRD Solution (n=470). Subsequently, 170 representative samples were used for the development and validation of an in-house HRD assay (MG_HRD), with external concordance assessed using the Myriad myChoice CDx assay in a subset of samples. Following validation, MG_HRD was implemented in routine clinical practice and applied to an independent cohort of 2,596 OC samples. HRD prevalence, BRCA mutation status, and clinicopathological associations were evaluated in all cohorts. Results: Among 4,163 ovarian cancer samples, HRD positivity was observed in 52.4% of cases, and pathogenic/likely pathogenic BRCA1/2 variants were identified in 23.6% of cases. Notably, 28.8% of tumors were BRCA wild-type but HRD-positive. BRCA-mutated tumors demonstrated significantly higher HRD genomic instability scores than BRCA wild-type tumors (p<0.001). HRD positivity was significantly enriched in high grade serous ovarian carcinomas. Remarkably, the BRCA1 c.68_69del (p.Glu23ValfsTer17) founder mutation was detected in 14.2% (97/685) of cases among the pathogenic variants in our study. The MG_HRD assay showed excellent concordance with commercial assays, achieving 97.1% overall agreement, 98.3% negative percent agreement (NPA), and 96.4% positive percent agreement (PPA), with complete concordance observed in the externally evaluated Myriad subset. Conclusions: This is the first Indian study to develop, validate, and implement an in-house HRD assay and evaluate HRD across three testing platforms in a large real-world OC cohort. The high prevalence of BRCA wild-type/HRD-positive tumors highlight the importance of comprehensive HRD testing, whereas the strong performance of MG_HRD supports its use as a reliable and cost-effective alternative for routine clinical practice. Keywords: ovarian cancer; homologous recombination deficiency; genomic instability, BRCA1/2, mutation, high grade serous carcinoma
n535d5639b022: Background: In multiple sclerosis (MS), dissemination in time (DIT) is an important component of demonstrating disease activity and establishing the chronology of lesion development. DIT is routinely assessed from contrast-enhanced or follow-up magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Although proved useful, these methods are not without caveats motivating alternative approaches to study lesion chronology. We investigated whether single T2-FLAIR MRI contains sufficient information to distinguish temporally distinct MS lesion categories using radiomic features. Methods: In a retrospective longitudinal cohort of 273 participants with MS (1,311 MRI acquisitions), persistent brain lesions were temporally stratified using serial T2-FLAIR MRI. Long-standing established (LS-E) lesions were defined as observed for six years at least, and recent incident (R-I), as lesions that appeared over the span of two years in a follow-up MRI and were present until the last scan available. Radiomic features were extracted from lesion-level T2-FLAIR MRI. Feature selection was performed in an independent discovery cohort (Group 1, N=55). Selected features were then used to train a support vector machine classifier in a separate development cohort with repeated group-wise cross-validation (Group 2, N=163). Final performance was assessed in an held-out test cohort (Group 3, N=55). An exploratory analysis was then performed on baseline MRI from 64 subjects with clinically isolated syndrome (CIS), acquired after their first clinical demyelinating event. Results: Longitudinal tracking identified 814 classifiable lesions in Group 1, 3203 in Group 2, and 984 in Group 3. In Group 1, 18 radiomic features met predefined selection criteria (FDR-adjusted p smaller than 0.05 and absolute Cohen's d greater than 0.8), spanning intensity, shape, and texture domains. In the independent test cohort, the support vector machine classifier achieved an area under the curve of 0.78, with correct classification rates of 66% for R-I lesions and 73% for LS-E lesions. In the exploratory CIS analysis, predicted lesion temporal composition showed substantial inter-patient heterogeneity, with approximately one in ten participants presenting radiomic features compatible with LS-E lesions at their first clinical event. Conclusions: Single T2-FLAIR MRI contains measurable information related to MS lesion chronology. This proof-of-concept framework supports the feasibility of a line of research based on radiomics temporal lesion characterisation without contrast administration or dense longitudinal follow-up MRI, with potential relevance for studying lesion evolution and supporting DIT assessment.
n644cad31e246: Background: Breastfeeding is a modifiable pathway contributing to infant health. Objectives: To estimate trajectories of breastfeeding and the association between trajectories of breastfeeding and infant health. Methods: We conducted a prospective longitudinal cohort study (2014-2020, Canada) with 3217 cohabitating English-literate mother-father-infant triads with internet or telephone access. Women with major psychiatric conditions or suicidality were excluded. Data were collected online at baseline (<3 weeks postpartum), 3, 6, 9, 12, 18, and 24 months. Breastfeeding was measured at 0-12 months. Baseline measures included attention-deficit disorder with/without hyperactivity (ADHD, Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale) and childhood adversity (Adverse Childhood Experiences International Questionnaire). We measured infant health at 12-24 months using the Brief Infant-Toddler Social and Emotional Assessment (challenging behaviors) and self-reported number of emergent visits (>90th percentile). We estimated trajectories of breastfeeding using latent class growth analysis. Associations were estimated using adjusted linear mixed models. Results: Most included mothers (n=2548) were of Canadian birth (2078/2548, 82%) and graduated from university (1920/2548, 75%); few reported unemployment (222/2548, 9%) or prenatal depression (240/2548, 9%). We identified two trajectories of breastfeeding: Constant Breastfeeding (1522/2548, 60%) and Decreasing Breastfeeding (1026/2548, 40%). No statistically significant differences were observed between classes for either the risk of challenging behaviors (RR -0.006 95% CI -0.028 to 0.016) or the risk of emergent visits (RR -0.015 95% CI -0.053 to 0.023). Conclusions: In this study, discontinued breastfeeding was not associated with infant health. Future studies should focus on 6-month exclusive breastfeeding, a modifiable therapeutic infant feeding target.
na3198b530788: Depression in adolescents has grown in prevalence in the past decade. Despite indications of differences in symptom presentation, measurement properties, and treatment response between adolescents and adults, research is dominated by adult participants. Qualitative work has identified symptomatic and functional domains important to depressed adolescents and those around them; however, there remains little quantitative evidence of how these domains relate to the functional impact of the disorder. In this preregistered study, we use adolescent self-report (n = 153) and parent-report (n = 106) responses in the depression section of the Development and Well-Being Assessment (DAWBA) to examine what information relevant to reported depression impact may be missing from its structured symptom-scale. We apply Large Language Models (LLMs) to participant free-text answers to extract information on a taxonomy of 80 outcomes. Through a sequential residual stacking framework that estimates incremental information in symptom sum-scores (S ), item-level symptom-scale answers (Q), and LLM-derived text representations (T ), we find that parent text contains information relevant to their report of depression impact that is not available in the structured symptom-scale, with the largest contributions concentrated in functioning-related domains (e.g., professional responsibilities, social exclusion, autonomy, coping). No such evidence was found in adolescent self-reports. Given the moderate sample size, these results are preliminary. Nonetheless, we provide a proof-of-concept framework for extracting information from open-ended free text in large existing datasets, and estimating incremental information across sources, which could be applied to uncover specific aspects of adolescent mental disorders across populations.
n2f47a4d709ba: Introduction: Peripheral neural injuries, known as polyneuropathy, are largely described in patients with Type-2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM). However, less is known about the T2DM-associated cerebral White Matter (WM) integrity. Previous studies highlighted mediating effects of inflammation in the T2DM-brain association. It is, however, still unclear whether Interleukin-6 (IL-6) mediates specifically T2DM-cerebral WM integrity. Methods: The multiethnic 50 years and older study population is a subset of the Health and Aging Brain Study: Health Disparities (HABS-HD) study. Diffusion-weighted scans were analyzed, and diffusion parameters were averaged in major WM tracts. Effect sizes (Cohen s d) were calculated after adjusting for relevant confounders. Mediation analysis was performed using 1000-fold non-parametric bootstrapping of 95% confidence intervals (CI). The results were adjusted for multiple testing using the False Discovery Rate method (FDR). Results: Several WM tracts showed significant impairment in T2DM participants after adjusting for confounders and multiple testing (posterior thalamic radiation (adj. Cohen s d=0.14[0.03-024]), anterior corona radiata (adj. Cohen s d=0.15[0.04-0.26]), cingulum (adj. Cohen s d=0.14[0.03-0.25]), inferior fronto-occipital fasciculus (adj. Cohen s d=0.16[0.06-0.27]), genu of the corpus callosum (adj. Cohen s d=0.13[0.03-0.24]), and body of the corpus callosum (adj. Cohen s d=0.28[0.17-0.38])). Within two years, the effect sizes showed an increasing trend. Even in cognitively unimpaired participants, T2DM was associated with locally reduced WM integrity. IL-6 statistically mediated up to 15% of these major associations. Conclusions: The study demonstrated T2DM-associated impairment of intracerebral WM integrity. In T2DM, microstructural WM changes might start before clinically objectified cognitive impairment. The role of systemic inflammation needs to be assessed in causal frameworks.
n7528ac102b73: Background Assessments of upper extremity control in ataxia are susceptible to measurement error and inherent variability. Objectives Quantify trial-to-trial variability in the Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (SARA) nose-to-finger (NTF) and finger chase (FC) tasks, and test agreement between scores derived from live assessment and retrospective video review. Methods 17 patients with cerebellar ataxia were video-recorded performing tasks behind a transparent, calibrated 1-cm grid. NTF tremor amplitude and FC undershoot/overshoot distance derived from live scores were compared with measurements from video review. Results NTF tremor amplitude and FC under/overshoot varied between consecutive trials. Patients received 2.4 {+/-} 0.7 (NTF) and 2.6 {+/-} 0.8 (FC) different SARA scores for limb excursions within one session. Live and video score match was NTF: 64.7% left, 70.6% right; FC: 64.7% left, 41.2% right. Live scoring often overestimated impairment. Conclusions Trial-to-trial variability and live/video discordance limit the precision of SARA upper-limb tasks.
ncafc2dd19045: Background Previous research has shown that clinical prediction models have likely been 'hacked' to meet arbitrary performance thresholds. However, this work only assessed abstracts, could not identify models with a perfect AUC (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve) of 1, and did not examine other performance metrics. Methods We collected data from full texts and validated a large language model to extract data from a random sample of Q1 journal articles for 2025. We examined if hacking occurred in the AUC value, sensitivity and specificity, and checked if articles correctly reported the AUC value from corresponding receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves. Results We identified 2,001 prediction model articles that reported 15,656 AUC values. We found a striking excess of results near perfect prediction and at multiples of five and ten for the AUC, sensitivity and specificity, indicating likely manipulated data, methods or publication bias. Around 1 in 40 AUC values were reported outside of their confidence intervals, and around 1 in 8 ROC curves did not match their reported AUC value. Conclusion We have shown that not only the AUC value, but the sensitivity and specificity are being hacked, likely to help the authors publish their paper at the cost of evidence for practice. Excess models that are not representative of their true performance may misguide clinicians, distort the literature, and make it harder to find prediction models that are useful for practice.
na0fd68b4d1a2: Background: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed cancer treatment, yet evidence on their utilization, treatment trajectories, and effectiveness in routine clinical practice remains limited. We characterized real-world ICI use and outcomes across cancer types using the multicenter FAIR-ICI cohort and explored differences between real-world and pivotal trial outcomes. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of adults receiving ICIs across four Belgian hospitals. Structured and unstructured electronic health record data were harmonized using the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership Common Data Model (OMOP-CDM) and natural language processing. We evaluated overall survival (OS), time on treatment (ToT), time to next treatment (TTNT), ICI discontinuation (>12-week treatment gap without re-initiation), and post-discontinuation survival. OS was descriptively compared with pivotal trials, and prognostic factors were assessed using multivariable Cox regression. An interactive public dashboard was developed to enable exploration of cohort characteristics, treatment patterns, and outcomes. Results: Among 3,231 ICI-treated patients, 2,514 (77.8%) had metastatic disease. Among metastatic patients, 568 (22.6%) discontinued ICI without subsequent systemic therapy. Median post-discontinuation OS was 21.4 months (95% CI 16.5-37.2), with 49.1% alive at 24 months. ToT and TTNT were generally shorter than OS, particularly in melanoma (median OS 78 months; ToT 7 months; TTNT 26 months). Real-world survival was frequently less favorable than in pivotal trials. ECOG >=2 was associated with poorer OS than ECOG 0-1 (adjusted HR 2.18, 95% CI 1.82-2.60). In NSCLC patients receiving pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy, survival with ECOG 0-1 more closely approximated trial outcomes, whereas survival with ECOG >=2 was substantially poorer. Conclusions: Real-world ICI treatment trajectories extend beyond active treatment, with some patients experiencing prolonged survival after discontinuation. Differences between real-world and trial outcomes highlight the importance of patient characteristics, particularly performance status, when interpreting trial evidence in routine care. FAIR-ICI provides a scalable framework for evaluating real-world immunotherapy effectiveness, treatment trajectories, and future investigations of treatment-related toxicity.
n74972a89a495: Background: High resolution respirometry of peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) is widely used to assess mitochondrial function, but reliance on freshly isolated cells limits flexibility and sample batching. The impact of cryopreservation and post-thaw handling on PBMC mitochondrial respiration remains incompletely defined. Methods: PBMCs from healthy young adults were analysed under three conditions: freshly isolated, cryopreserved and directly thawed, and cryopreserved followed by overnight recovery in supplemented culture medium. Mitochondrial respiration was assessed using an Oroboros O2k high-resolution respirometer following plasma membrane permeabilisation and a substrate uncoupler inhibitor titration protocol. Respiration parameters included leak, oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), maximal uncoupled respiration, and non-mitochondrial oxygen consumption. Results: Directly thawed PBMCs exhibited reduced ATP-coupled and maximal respiratory flux compared with fresh cells, indicating acute cryopreservation-induced mitochondrial suppression. In contrast, PBMCs undergoing overnight recovery showed substantial restoration of mitochondrial function, with OXPHOS and uncoupled respiration closely approximating those of fresh cells. Cell viability was comparable across conditions. Conclusion: Cryopreserved PBMCs can be reliably used for mitochondrial respirometry when an overnight recovery step is included. This approach enables sample storage, batching, and broader application in large-scale and retrospective human studies.
n7545dff34c28: Trachoma is the leading infectious cause of blindness worldwide and is targeted for global elimination as a public health problem by 2030. As we approach this target, defining when population-level trachoma control interventions can be stopped, and determining how post-intervention surveillance should be performed, are becoming increasingly important. Molecular diagnosis of ocular Chlamydia trachomatis (Ct) using polymerase chain reaction (PCR) provides a highly sensitive and specific indicator of infection, yet there are currently no programmatic guidelines based on Ct infection. We assembled 86 cross-sectional surveys of ocular Ct infection from 13 countries, representing data from 46,914 children aged 1-5 years. Our analyses suggest that infection prevalence of 0.81% in this age group corresponds to a threshold below which population-level interventions can be stopped with at least 90% confidence. Correspondingly, with confidence exceeding 90%, we propose that interventions should continue when infection prevalence is greater than 1.99%. Interpretation of infection surveillance data is a generalisable challenge in low-prevalence settings for many infectious diseases. This study proposes a robust framework for how Ct infection surveillance could support accurate population-level assessments of trachoma endemicity and could allow a step-change in decision-making precision for programmes as we approach the endgame for trachoma elimination.
n19f0baf69596: The COVID-19 pandemic highlighted the importance of widespread, accessible viral surveillance to ensure pandemic-preparedness. The rapid diagnosis of respiratory infections is crucial not only for effective patient management but also to inform ongoing surveillance for the detection of outbreaks. Reverse transcriptase-Loop mediated isothermal amplification (RT-LAMP) assays are an attractive alternative to reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) for rapid, decentralised testing in resource limited settings due being rapid and low cost. Here we present the design and evaluation of a multiplexed RT-LAMP assay for the simultaneous detection of SARS-CoV-2, Influenza A and Respiratory Syncytial Virus via the incorporation of fluorescently labelled LAMP probes. Mid-nasal swabs collected from 175 participants on the day of enrolment in the MALCOV Cohort study in Kisumu, Kenya were used in the evaluation of the RT-LAMP assay. Overall, 114 SARS-CoV-2, six Influenza A, two Influenza B and zero RSV samples were identified in the cohort by the Allplex SARS-CoV-2/FluA/FluB/RSV RT-PCR kit (Seegene Inc) reference test, in addition to 53 negatives. Sensitivity and specificity of the RT-LAMP assay (SARS-CoV-2/FluA/RSV) when compared to RT-PCR was 82.64% [CI95%:74.70-88.92%] and 100% [CI95%:93.40-100%] at 40 minutes for all samples respectively. The mean time to a positive result was 11minutes, highlighting the speed of this technology compared to the more commonly used RT-PCR. RT-LAMP enables rapid multi-pathogen detection with comparable diagnostic accuracy to RT-PCR.
n73933a062a84: Objective: For the atypical parkinsonian disorders (APDs), including dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), multiple system atrophy (MSA), progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), and corticobasal degeneration (CBD), accurate antemortem diagnosis remains clinically challenging because of overlapping features, phenotypic heterogeneity, and limited definitive biomarkers. Consensus diagnostic criteria are complex and may not reflect how clinicians operationalize diagnostic reasoning in practice. Methods: We surveyed movement disorders specialists regarding diagnostic implications of 32 clinical features, comparing the results with a 2024 consensus algorithmic framework called the "General Neurologist's Practical Diagnostic Algorithm for APDs". We evaluated inter-rater agreement, diagnosis-level framework coverage, feature-level attribution patterns, and exact-set agreement. Results: Respondents demonstrated strong inter-specialist consensus in feature attribution (raw agreement 81.9%; Gwet's AC1 0.67, 95% CI 0.64-0.70). Specialist endorsement increased markedly with framework association strength, from 12.9% to 36.2% to 82.6% for unmapped, modest, and moderate associations respectively. Diagnosis-level coverage was higher for MSA, PSP, and CBD than for DLB. Exact-set agreement was substantially more variable and depended on whether modest associations were incorporated into the framework definition. Despite high self-reported familiarity with and use of published diagnostic criteria, respondents overwhelmingly expressed interest in a unified diagnostic framework for APDs with automated clinical decision support (CDS). Conclusions: Movement disorders specialists showed internally consistent feature-attribution patterns for archetypal features, while differing in the weighting and breadth assigned to weaker or overlapping associations. These findings are evidence for a gap between consensus schemas and specialist diagnostic reasoning and may inform future diagnostic frameworks and CDS approaches for the APDs.
nd3f91fad1e12: Background: Sex differences in sudden cardiac arrest (SCA) incidence and outcomes are well established, but risk stratification underperforms in women. It is important to delineate sex-specific patterns in SCA across clinical, electrocardiographic, and echocardiographic domains. Methods: We studied out-of-hospital SCA cases from the Oregon Sudden Unexpected Death Study (ORSUDS; Portland, 2002-2020; discovery) and Prediction of Sudden Death in Multi-Ethnic Communities (PRESTO; Ventura County, 2015-2024; external replication). Sex differences in 38 comorbidities, 19 ECG and 12 echocardiographic measures were estimated using multivariable-adjusted logistic regression. Female sex was the modeled dependent measure (male as reference). ORSUDS estimates were compared with those in the Framingham Heart Study (FHS), a community-based reference cohort, using FDR-adjusted Cochran Q tests. Results: Among 5130 ORSUDS cases, 1715 (33.4%) were women (median age, 70.4 years [IQR, 58.7-81.8]) and 3415 (66.6%) were men (65.6 [55.0-76.8]). Compared with men, women had higher BMI (per 5 kg/m2, 1.11 [1.08-1.15]) and higher odds of thyroid disease (2.56 [2.17-3.13]), asthma (2.33 [1.92-2.86]), mood disorder (2.17 [1.85-2.50]), dementia (1.27 [1.02-1.56]), and left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH, 3.13 [2.44-4.00]). Women also had lower odds of coronary artery disease (0.61 [0.52-0.71]), atrial fibrillation (0.67 [0.56-0.79]), prolonged QTc (0.45 [0.35-0.57]), prolonged PR (0.53 [0.41-0.68]), premature contractions (0.77 [0.60-0.98]), sleep apnea (0.53 [0.43-0.65]), and reduced LVEF (0.40 [0.29-0.54]). Most findings were replicated in PRESTO (n=2719). In contrast, several of these differences were reversed in the community (FHS, n=3539;FDR-significant): prolonged QTc was more common in women, whereas LVH, dementia, heart failure, and higher BMI were more common in men. Conclusions: Sex differences among SCA cases were mostly reproducible in SCA cohorts, and distinct from sex-related patterns in the community. These results have implications for development of sex-specific SCA risk assessment and prevention strategies.
n72696517b12a: Background A recent international randomized trial found that the proton pump inhibitor (PPI) pantoprazole significantly reduced the risk of clinically important upper gastrointestinal (GI) bleeding among invasively ventilated patients in the intensive care unit (ICU), with no effect on mortality. Pantoprazole may be of particularly high utility among patients at high-risk of bleeding, such as those receiving renal replacement therapy (RRT) prior to ICU admission. However, given the complex mechanisms by which renal insufficiency may increase bleeding risk, as well as the possible association between PPI use and adverse kidney outcomes, investigating whether kidney failure treated with RRT at baseline modifies the treatment effect of PPIs is clinically relevant. Methods We have planned a post hoc secondary analysis of the Re-evaluating the Inhibition of Stress Erosions (REVISE) Trial ( NCT03374800 ). The primary objective if this study is to evaluate whether any RRT on study day 1 (e.g., maintenance RRT in the outpatient setting, or RRT initiated in the hospital [intermittent hemodialysis, continuous renal replacement therapy, sustained low efficiency dialysis, or peritoneal dialysis]) modifies the treatment effect of pantoprazole on clinically important upper GI bleeding and 90-day mortality. The secondary objective is to evaluate whether maintenance RRT (intermittent hemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis) in an outpatient setting before the index hospital admission modifies the effect of pantoprazole on clinically important upper GI bleeding and 90-day mortality. Secondary outcomes for both analyses are patient important upper GI bleeding, ICU and hospital mortality. We will perform Cox proportional-hazard analyses, including the RRT exposure of interest, randomized group, and their interaction for each outcome, reporting results as hazards ratios with 95% confidence intervals, and p-values for the interaction term. Conclusion Results of this study will inform critical care practice, particularly for the care of patients at risk of stress-related GI ulceration in the ICU who have received RRT.
nd6be287e48a1: Aims/hypothesis Glycated albumin (GA) has been shown to be a moderate predictor of gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), while evidence supporting its role in predicting adverse pregnancy outcomes remains limited. Here, we aimed to perform a comparative study of GA and haemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) for predicting GDM and large-for-gestational-age (LGA) infants in a prospective cohort. Methods We developed a rapid liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry method for measuring site-specific albumin glycation. GA was quantified at two glycation sites, GA (KQT) and GA (KLV), as well as their sum, GA-total. GA was measured in stored serum samples collected at 11-14 and 23-31 gestational weeks from 465 participants in the single-centre observational cohort. HbA1c was measured routinely at each visit. Linear mixed-effects models were used to compare GA between participants with and without GDM (n=100) or LGA (n=57). Logistic regression was used to estimate odds ratios (ORs) for GDM and LGA according to GA and HbA1c. Results GA was lower in women who developed GDM during early pregnancy compared to non-GDM controls (GA-total; p=0.004), while in mid-late pregnancy, only GA (KQT) was lower in women with GDM (p=0.036). In contrast, HbA1c was higher in women with GDM at both timepoints compared to non-GDM controls (p<0.001) and higher HbA1c was associated with increased odds of GDM (OR=2.20, p<0.001; OR=2.30, p<0.001, respectively). GA was higher in the LGA group, in both early (GA-total; p=0.032) and mid-late pregnancy (GA-total; p=0.030) and associated with increased odds of LGA (GA-total; OR=1.59, p=0.009; GA-total; OR=1.46, p=0.019, respectively). HbA1c was not associated with LGA at either timepoint. Conclusions/interpretation Higher GA in early and mid-late pregnancy were associated with an increased risk of LGA, whereas no significant association was observed for HbA1c. GA may therefore provide risk assessment beyond HbA1c for identifying pregnancies at risk of fetal overgrowth.
nc55680d305af: Background: Cognitive training (CogT) is an established non-pharmacological intervention for people with Parkinson's disease (PD) and mild cognitive impairment (PD-MCI). However, overall effects on cognitive outcomes are small to moderate and interindividually highly heterogeneous. Sleep -especially deep sleep- could be an important determinant of CogT responsiveness in PD, and may have beneficial effects on PD pathophysiology. Therefore, the enhancement of deep sleep by phase-targeted auditory stimulation (PTAS) could strengthen the effects of CogT on cognitive symptoms and counteract disease progression. Methods: PD-CogT-Sleep is a monocentric, partly decentralized, double-blind, randomized sham-controlled trial that combines two remotely delivered non-pharmacological interventions, to assess the additive effect of PTAS on digital CogT responsiveness in people with PD-MCI. The primary outcome is executive functions; Secondary and exploratory outcomes include further cognitive functions, participant-reported outcome measures, blood-based biomarkers, and high-density sleep electroencephalography markers. Outcomes are assessed at baseline, five weeks post-allocation and at 3-month follow-up. We aim to consecutively recruit N=50 participants, who will be randomized 1:1 to receive CogT+PTAS or CogT+Sham. Discussion: The PD-CogT-Sleep study integrates wearable and digital technologies to systematically combine a novel, non-invasive, sleep-enhancing intervention (PTAS) with established CogT to improve cognition and evaluate PTAS' disease-modifying potential through its effects on blood-based biomarkers in PD-MCI. The expected results will foster our understanding of the interplay of sleep, cognition, and neurodegeneration, and may guide further development of safe, feasible, scalable, patient-centered, technology-based non-pharmacological interventions counteracting cognitive decline in neurodegenerative diseases.
ne5ec484c241e: Observational studies using electronic health records are being increasingly used to answer research questions of interest in deprescribing, where a medication is intentionally discontinued or the dose reduced. Target trial emulation (TTE) is particularly attractive as it is guided by sound theoretical principles based on causal inference. In the field of deprescribing, the evaluation of TTE within a simulation setting can provide evidence on optimal approaches for implementation and compare different estimation approaches which theory cannot easily inform. Deprescribing studies are susceptible to time-dependent confounding, competing risks due to early adverse events, time-dependent effects and other data complexities which may render estimates biased if such aspects are not properly addressed. In this work, a Monte-Carlo simulation study was conducted to estimate the performance (bias and coverage) of seven methods within several synthetic data generating mechanisms involving the above characteristics. The methods implemented were Cox regression, inverse probability of treatment weighted (IPTW) Cox regression, naive sequential Cox regression, IPTW weighted sequential Cox regression, extended Cox regression and the parametric g-formula. The IPTW Cox regression and IPTW sequential Cox regression were the only methods achieving nominal coverage and unbiasedness under the scenarios evaluated.
n33fdcd244a68: Objectives: Fibromuscular dysplasia (FMD) is a non inflammatory, non atherosclerotic arterial disease characterized by multifocal arterial beading that predominantly affects women. Although FMD commonly involves the renal and carotid arteries, its relationship with acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) remains poorly understood. We investigated the proportion of patients with FMD among patients with ATAAD, focusing on sex based differences. Materials and Methods: Patients aged below 70 years with ATAAD and ECG triggered aortic CT angiography (CTA) were consecutively included in this retrospective single-center study. FMD was defined as multifocal arterial beading (string-of-beads appearance) in at least one vascular territory, according to international consensus criteria. The highest-quality CTA examination was evaluated by an experienced cardiovascular radiologist. All suspected FMD cases were independently reviewed by a second experienced cardiovascular radiologist, with the final diagnosis established by consensus. Proportions were reported with 95% confidence intervals and compared between sexes . Results: Of 214 patients screened, 200 were included (138 men and 62 women). FMD was confirmed in 18/200 patients (9%; 95% CI, 6 till 14%), none of whom had a prior FMD diagnosis. FMD was more frequent in women (12/62, 19%; 95% CI, 11 till 31%) than men (6/138, 4%; 95% CI, 2 till 9%; P<0.001). FMD predominantly involved the renal arteries. Additional carotid CTA was available in 49/200 patients (25%) and in 7/18 patients with FMD (39%); three of these seven patients had carotid FMD. Conclusion: FMD was observed in a substantial proportion of patients presenting with ATAAD, particularly women. These findings suggest that FMD is an underrecognized vascular phenotype in patients with ATAAD.
n7af1f9f9f589: We find that a vast space of public health interventions necessarily reshape the intervals between successive infections, known as generation times, for directly-transmitted infectious diseases (e.g., COVID-19, Ebola virus, influenza). While some studies have connected specific interventions (e.g., contact-tracing, isolation) to shifted generation times, most epidemiological analyses assume these intervals are stationary. We reveal that this assumption is substantially more fragile than previously recognised. We develop a universal microscopic representation for all intervention mechanisms that reduce individual-level infectiousness and establish generation-time reshaping as a fundamental macroscopic feature of those interventions, emerging at the population level. By constraining the topology of our representation to reflect specific mechanisms, we explain and unify previous studies as well as predict generation-time phenomena yet to be observed. We further show that neglecting generation-time reshaping can under- or over-estimate intervention effectiveness and disease control- lability by 100%, under realistic parameter settings. A stringent intervention can even produce no estimated transmissibility difference. Generation-time distortion causes unavoidable and underrated biases that can severely limit model-driven public health policy and pandemic preparedness.
n850c3749f50e: Background: Low haemoglobin concentration, or anaemia, is a major global public health issue, particularly severe in sub-Saharan Africa, including East Africa, where prevalence rates are alarmingly high. This situation requires a comprehensive analysis to identify the key factors contributing to this high prevalence, especially in East Africa. This study uses robust quantile regression to examine the relationship between maternal haemoglobin concentration and child haemoglobin levels in three East African countries. Methods: The study analysed data from the Demographic and Health Surveys of three East African countries: Ethiopia, Tanzania, and Uganda. These data are nationally representative and are collected every five years from low- and middle-income countries. The analysis included a total sample of 6883 children and their mothers. The primary outcome variable was the haemoglobin concentration of the child. We used quantile regression to model the effects of maternal haemoglobin concentration on child haemoglobin levels, adjusting for potential confounders. Results: A one-unit increase in maternal haemoglobin concentration was associated with a unit increase in child haemoglobin concentration as follows: In Tanzania, the increases were 0.19, 0.20, 0.19, and 0.17 at the 5th, 10th, 25th, and 50th quantiles, respectively. In Ethiopia, the increases were 0.23, 0.22, 0.22, and 0.17 at the same quantiles. In Uganda, the increases were 0.19, 0.19, 0.18, and 0.19 at these quantiles. In contrast, a one-unit increase in maternal Hb concentration was associated with a smaller increase in child haemoglobin concentration, ranging from 0.11 to 0.13 at the 75th and 90th quantiles across all three countries. Overall, the most significant effects of maternal Hb concentration on child Hb levels were observed at the lower end of the conditional Hb distribution in each of the three countries. Conclusion: Maternal haemoglobin concentration is positively associated with children's haemoglobin levels across all countries studied. The strongest association is among children in the lower quantiles, who are at higher risk of anaemia. In contrast, the association is less pronounced among those in the upper quantiles. Therefore, improving maternal haemoglobin is likely to benefit children in the lower quantiles more than those in the upper quantiles. Programmes aimed at addressing child anaemia should consider these differing effects of maternal haemoglobin concentration. Keywords: Haemoglobin concentration, anaemia, maternal, child, quantile regression
nd9ab6ecf0441: Hospitals globally are under increasing strain due to rising demand and constrained capacity. This interrupted-time-series study evaluates the impact of a digital coordination centre, implemented on August 28th of 2023, where a multidisciplinary operational team (comprising data scientists, patient flow managers, facilities managers, patient transport and nursing staff, for example) use real-time data dashboards showing measures of emergency department (ED) crowding and inpatient utilisation to optimise patient flow in an Australian metropolitan tertiary hospital. Analysis of 191,415 emergency department arrivals admitted to acute care and 187,783 acute inpatient episodes between July 2020 and July 2025 showed substantial improvements in measures of patient flow: 33% decrease in ED length of stay, 73% increase in hospital admissions from the ED within four hours of arrival, 7% decrease in inpatient length of stay, and 5% increase in discharges completed before noon. These changes coincided with a broader programme of organisational and operational reform, of which the DCC was a central integrating component. Hence, the findings support digitally enabled coordination centres as an effective contribution the overall strategy for improving hospital operational efficiency.
n85a12f573eb3: Objectives: Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) offers alternative options to patients with Obstructive Sleep Apnea (OSA) unable to tolerate first line treatment. Randomized controlled trial data suggest efficacy of NMES treatment in improving OSA outcomes, snoring and sleepiness; however, no study to our knowledge has examined the effects on a range of daytime patient reported outcomes in a large real-world sample. Methods: This report presents clinical data from 472 patients completing NMES treatment. Bayesian linear mixed models were used to analyze pre-to-post treatment changes in mood (PHQ8), sleep disturbance (PROMIS-SD-4a), sleep related impairment (PROMIS-SRI-4a), and functioning (FOSQ), whilst controlling for key covariates. Posterior probabilities were calculated to estimate the probability of a change in symptoms (P(effect > 0)) and probability of exceeding a minimal clinically important difference (P(effect > MCID)). Results: The posterior probabilities of an improvement in scores in sleep disturbance (mean change -6.1, 94% HDI: -3.8 to -8.5) and sleep-related impairment (mean change -10.0, 94% HDI: -5.4 to -14), depression (mean change -3.5, 94% HDI: -1.7 to -5.2), at posttreatment were greatest and varied between 99.8 to 100%. Probability of change in functioning was low (60.9% chance of improvement). These effects remained when controlling for age, gender, treatment adherence, mean intensity and variance in intensity. Probabilities for MCI change for mood, sleep disturbance and sleep-related impairment were high (86-91%). Conclusions: The results from this report highlight the potential impact NMES therapy has on patient reported outcomes. These findings are in support of prior randomized placebo-controlled data and several observational cohort studies for NMES as treatment for mild OSA.
nc87fc39f1746: Background: Dementia is frequently underdiagnosed in primary care, with fewer than half of cases identified and only 8-20% detected at early stages. Our objective is to develop an Agentic AI-powered clinical decision support systems (CDSS) maintaining the patient's virtual cognitive status and provide physicians with ready-to-use summaries and next step suggestions. Methods: We developed MERIT (Multi-agent EHR-grounded Risk Identification and Tailored Care for Early Cognitive Decline in Primary Care) via participatory co-design with primary care provider. It maintains a virtual cognitive status based on the patient's electronic health records (EHR) and conversation with the patient and provide clinical decision support based on it. Retrieval augmented generation (RAG) was employed by the system to retrieve dementia-related risk factors from multimodal EHR. Additionally, we used reflection Agentic AI design pattern to improve quality of AI Agent generated text. We used one PCP's patient data to optimize the system, then used patients from another four PCPs for testing. We mainly used expert manual evaluation based on 5-point Likert-Scales. For readability of patient summary and personalized education material, besides manual evaluation, we also employed widely used Flesch Reading Ease and Flesch We-Kincaid Grade Level. Results: MERIT has four modulars: 1) patient conversation agent; 2) patient virtual cognitive status maintainer; 3) personalized education provider; and 4) decision support provider. Our evaluation focused on the provider-facing part, which relies on EHR without involving any patient conversation. The evaluation on the testing data demonstrates good performance. On a 5-point Likert scale, in the test set, patient virtual cognitive status summaries received average scores of 4.0 (SD 0.74) for correctness, 4.2 (SD 0.59) for completeness, 4.3 (SD 0.59) for readability, and 4.1 (SD 0.71) for clinical usefulness; clinical decision support received 3.9 (SD 0.87) for correctness, 4.3 (SD 0.66) for completeness, and 4.3 (SD 0.64) for adoptability; and the personalized education material received average ratings of 4.3 (SD 0.62) for completeness, 4.5 (SD 0.60) for readability, 4.3 (SD 0.78) for usefulness, and 4.4 (SD 0.49) for empathy. Automated readability assessment showed that patient summaries had a mean Flesch Reading Ease score of 18.3 (SD 4.9) and a Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of 13.7 (SD 0.7), consistent with college-level text, whereas personalized patient education had a Flesch Reading Ease score of 50.1 (SD 7.1) and a Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level of 11.7 (SD 1.5), which is high-school student understandable text. Conclusion: Our developed system MERIT can maintain a virtual cognitive status based on the patient's multimodal EHR, provide the patient with clear and readable personalized education materials, and provide the PCP with ready-to-use cognitive summaries and decision support with high adoptability. By integrating our CDSS into Epic in the near future, our developed system will largely benefit older adults with cognitive decline and slow down the progression.
n729e6587ae26: Importance: Maternal attention-deficit disorder with or without hyperactivity (ADHD) is an established risk factor for adverse perinatal outcomes that remains understudied to breastfeeding. Objective: To estimate the effect of maternal ADHD on 6-month exclusive breastfeeding. Design: A prospective longitudinal community-based cohort study. Setting: Canada, 2014-2020. Participants: We included 3217 English-literate mother-father dyads with internet or telephone access, comprising women with singleton birth within 3 weeks postpartum (study baseline) and were cohabiting with the biological father. Women with major psychiatric conditions or suicidality were excluded. All participants provided informed consent at recruitment. Data were collected online through self-report questionnaires. Exposure: Maternal ADHD was measured at baseline using the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (sum of scores [≥]14). Main Outcomes and Measures: We defined 6-month exclusive breastfeeding based on maternal reported infant feeding, assessed at 3 and 6 months. Maternal childhood adversity (Adverse Childhood Experiences International Questionnaire, ACE-IQ; sum score) was included as a confounder. The average treatment effect on the treated (ATT) was estimated using linear probability models. We calculated 95% percentile bootstrap CI. Missing data were handled using multiple imputation by chained equations with 10 iterations. Results: Complete-case analyses included 2071/3217 mother-father dyads, most of which were Canadian-born (79%). Childhood adversity, mental health conditions, and substance use were higher among mothers who screened positive for ADHD (4%) than among those who did not: the median number of ACE was 5 IQR 4-6; 38% self-reported prenatal depression, 13% smoked cigarettes and 19% drank alcohol during pregnancy; 11% of infants used the neonatal intensive care unit. Notably, though 90% of mothers with ADHD intended to breastfeed exclusively only 28% breastfed exclusively for 6 months. Among families with maternal ADHD, the effect of maternal ADHD on 6-month exclusive breastfeeding was ATT -0.105, 95% CI -0.209 to -0.003 in the model adjusted for maternal ACE and paternal ADHD. With multiple imputation: ATT -0.109, 95% CI -0.213 to -0.004. Conclusions and Relevance: Mothers with ADHD intend to breastfeed their infants exclusively, but additional challenges shorten the duration of exclusive breastfeeding, indicating a need for interventions tailored to neurodevelopmental differences.
n627c5f011d00: Background: Diarrhoea remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality among children under five. WHO and UNICEF recommend oral rehydration salts (ORS) alongside 10 to 14 days of zinc supplementation. However, national progress in combined treatment coverage and its socioeconomic and care-related inequalities remains insufficiently understood in Bangladesh. We assessed combined coverage, wealth inequality and differences by reported source of care. Methods: We analysed children under five with caregiver-reported diarrhoea in the 2019 (n=1,589) and 2025 (n=1,634) Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys (MICS). We estimated combined coverage using design-based methods, wealth inequality using slope indices, and associations with source of care using pooled adjusted prevalence ratios (aPR). Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) estimates provided an external comparison. Results: Combined ORS and zinc coverage increased from 35.0% (95% CI 32.3 to 37.7) in 2019 to 42.9% (40.1 to 45.8) in 2025. In 2025, ORS and zinc coverage were 75.8% and 51.9%, respectively. The 2025 estimate agreed with DHS 2022, whereas MICS 2019 was below DHS 2017-18. Wealth inequality persisted in 2025 (slope index 13.0 percentage points, 3.4 to 22.6). Adjustment attenuated the pooled slope index from 11.8 to 6.5 points (-1.7 to 14.6). Coverage was lower with pharmacy-only than public care (aPR 0.59, 0.53 to 0.66) and with no care reported (0.14, 0.11 to 0.18). Children with no care reported accounted for 43.7% of children without combined treatment in 2025. Conclusions: Combined coverage increased, although the apparent progress may be overstated by the lower MICS 2019 estimate relative to DHS. Zinc remained the larger treatment gap, while one in four children received no ORS. Reported sources of care require cautious interpretation.
nc52e23eac8ac: RATIONALE AND OBJECTIVES 3D-TOF-MRA is a standard non-invasive method for detecting and monitoring intracranial aneurysms, but long scan times remain a limitation. Compressed sensing (CS) acceleration for intracranial aneurysm evaluation has mainly been studied at 3T. This prospective single-center non-inferiority study compared CS-accelerated 3D-TOF at 1.5T with GRAPPA-accelerated 3D-TOF-MRA for evaluating untreated intracranial aneurysms. MATERIALS AND METHODS Sample size was determined via a preliminary retrospective study. 25 patients with 32 untreated aneurysms underwent both CS- (factor 7, 3:04 min) and GRAPPA-accelerated (factor 2, 5:00 min) 3D-TOF, yielding a 38.7% scan-time reduction. Two blinded neuroradiologists assessed overall image quality (primary endpoint) and artifacts, subjective CNR, aneurysm delineation and diameters (secondary endpoints). Non-inferiority was tested via one-sided t-test (prespecified 10% margin); interrater agreement used ICC. RESULTS CS demonstrated non-inferiority to GRAPPA for overall image quality in both readers (p <= .023), though interrater agreement was low (ICC 0.241-0.262), reflecting subjective variability. Secondary exploratory analyses showed heterogeneous preferences. ROI-based CNR was lower for CS (median 169.6; IQR, 91.0-226. vs. 278.2; 181.0-366.2). Aneurysm diameter measurements showed excellent interrater agreement for both techniques (CS ICC, 0.899-0.980; GRAPPA ICC, 0.877-0.973; all p < .001). CONCLUSION CS-accelerated 3D-TOF at 1.5T met non-inferiority criteria vs. GRAPPA-TOF for overall image quality, reducing scan time by 38.7% while preserving aneurysm measurement reliability. However, reduced CNR and reader-preference variability important trade-offs.
nede41b94451f: Background: Postoperative delirium is a common perioperative complication. Early randomised trials suggested that non-invasive brain stimulation may reduce postoperative delirium, whereas the recent MODEST trial found no preventive benefit. We synthesised the randomised evidence for perioperative non-invasive brain stimulation. Methods: We searched eight bibliographic databases and ClinicalTrials.gov from inception to 30 September 2026 for randomised controlled trials of perioperative non-invasive brain stimulation in adults undergoing surgery. The primary outcome was postoperative delirium. Random-effects meta-analyses estimated risk ratios (RRs), mean differences, or standardised mean differences. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2 and certainty of evidence using GRADE. Results: Nine trials contributed data from 1451 participants. Postoperative delirium occurred in 72 of 750 participants receiving active stimulation and 166 of 701 controls (RR 0.41, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.31-0.56; I2=24.7%; moderate-certainty evidence). Estimates also favoured stimulation for hypoactive and hyperactive delirium, but not clearly for mixed delirium. Pain, anxiety, and sleep outcomes favoured stimulation but were highly heterogeneous and supported by very-low-certainty evidence. Length of hospital stay was not reduced. Adverse events could not be pooled because reporting was incomplete and inconsistent. Conclusions: Perioperative non-invasive brain stimulation may reduce postoperative delirium, but the evidence does not establish a class effect or support routine clinical use. Geographical concentration, methodological concerns, heterogeneous stimulation protocols, and discordance with the MODEST trial warrant independent multicentre sham-controlled trials. PROSPERO registration: CRD420261522168 Keywords: meta-analysis; non-invasive brain stimulation; perioperative neurocognitive disorders; postoperative delirium; transcranial direct current stimulation; transcranial magnetic stimulation
na6651b4831ba: Objective: Drug use after trauma is common, but polydrug use patterns, motives, and associations with subsequent symptoms are poorly understood. We examined these associations among mass-casualty terror attack survivors, 72% of whom used drugs immediately before trauma exposure. Methods: Survivors of the October 7, 2023 Nova Festival attack reported use of six drug types (alcohol, cannabis, ketamine, stimulants, MDMA, psychedelics) and motives (avoidance, emotional regulation, self-medication, sleep, recreation) longitudinally at three timepoints (TP): 1-6 months (N=772), 8-12 months (N=453), and 17-24 months (N=302) post-attack. Separate latent class analyses of TP2 data characterized drug use, motives, and their combination. Linear regression and mixed-effects models examined associations between class membership and PTSD Checklist for DSM-5 (PCL-5) scores, adjusting for age, sex, time since trauma, and TP1 PCL-5 scores. Results: At TP2, 70% reported polydrug use, 17% used one drug, and 13% reported no use. The high drug-load class (mean 4.6 drug types) had lower PCL-5 scores than the low drug-load class (mean 1.5 drug types); this difference was evident among participants using [≥]4 drug types and persisted through TP3. The self-medication-motive class had higher PCL-5 scores than the recreational-motive class. In joint analyses, recreational-motive users at both low and high drug loads had lower PCL-5 scores than participants reporting self-medication motives and primarily cannabis use. Conclusions: Polydrug use was common among the mass-trauma survivors in our study. Self-medication motives were associated with higher PTSD symptom severity than recreational motives. Unexpectedly, higher polydrug use was associated with lower PTSD symptom scores.
n9227358b3e35: Background: Perimenopause is a transitional stage preceding menopause, characterized by hormonal fluctuations and physiological changes that may increase cardiometabolic risk. Emerging evidence suggests that the gut microbiome may influence these changes through estrogen metabolism and microbial metabolite production. Inulin, a prebiotic fiber that modulates the gut microbiome, may offer a targeted nutritional strategy; however, its effects during perimenopause remain largely unexplored. Objective: This proof-of-concept study evaluates the effects of short-term inulin supplementation on gut microbiome composition, microbial metabolites, vascular function, skeletal muscle health, and metabolic flexibility in perimenopausal overweight women or with obesity. Methods: We will conduct a randomized, blinded, placebo-controlled crossover trial among 27 women aged 40 to55 years. Participants will receive 10 g/day of inulin and a matched maltodextrin placebo for two 14-day intervention periods separated by a 2 to 4-week washout. We will assess changes in gut and vaginal microbiome composition and functional capacity, stool and plasma microbial metabolites, and circulating markers of estrogen metabolism as primary outcomes. We will also evaluate vascular function, skeletal muscle health and oxidative capacity, and metabolic flexibility as secondary outcomes. Additionally, we will assess physical activity, sleep, dietary intake, perimenopausal symptoms, and intervention feasibility, adherence, acceptability, and tolerability. Conclusion: This study will provide novel insights into the feasibility and biological effects of inulin supplementation on gut-host mechanisms and cardiometabolic health during perimenopause, informing the design of future larger-scale trials. Keywords: Gut Microbiome, Metabolome, Fiber, Women, Prebiotics, Clinical Trial Protocol, Inulin, Perimenopause, Healthy Aging
n1ce33d574204: Background and Objectives: Motor dysfunction is a major contributor to disability in pediatric-onset monogenic neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), yet systematic quantifications of motor phenotypes across development using validated clinical scales remain underdeveloped. Existing studies have classified motor phenotypes rather than quantified domain-specific severity, limiting their use as outcome measures in clinical trials. Here, we systematically quantify motor dysfunction using established clinical rating scales to explore their utility as motor endpoints. Methods: In this cross-sectional observational study, 102 individuals with NDDs (0.5-38 years) secondary to pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants in five genes (SCN2A, KCNQ2, CSNK2A1, CACNA1A, SCN8A) and 31 unaffected sibling controls underwent standardized motor assessments using the Scale for Assessment and Rating of Ataxia, Burke-Fahn-Marsden Dystonia Scale, and the Modified Ashworth Scale. Regional and functional categorization of parameters enabled differentiated interpretation. Gene-specific patterns were evaluated using z-score standardization across the pooled affected cohort, with gene-level averaging and nonparametric bootstrap-derived 95% confidence intervals. Results: Dysfunction was present in individuals with NDDs across speech (90%), coordination (87%), dystonia (83.3%), gross motor (82.4%) and spasticity (42.2%), with minimal impairment in controls (0-12.9%). We observed substantial heterogeneity across motor domains and subdomains; ataxic dysarthria had the highest score distribution (median 0.83 [IQR, 0.17-1.0]), whereas spasticity showed near-floor scores. Individuals with SCN2A variants demonstrated higher mean z-scores across multiple subdomains than other genes, with more consistent deviations observed in coordination and speech domains (Coordination: mean z = 0.29, 95% CI 0.03-0.54; Speech: mean z = 0.3, 95% CI 0.03-0.57), whereas domain-specific or less pronounced patterns were observed in other genes. The ataxia and dystonia scales demonstrated low floor and ceiling effects. Discussion: Using three clinical scales across a broad developmental and functional range, our study moves motor phenotyping in monogenic NDDs from categorical description toward quantitative, domain-resolved severity assessment. Exploratory analysis indicates marked heterogeneity in severity profiles across genes, most notably in SCN2A, suggesting potential selective motor vulnerability. These findings provide evidence for the feasibility of motor phenotyping and provide preliminary, cross-sectional benchmark severity distributions. Subsequent longitudinal validation and validation in larger, longitudinal, and variant-stratified cohorts will enable natural history studies and future therapeutic trials alongside seizure outcomes.
nf531a0f49c10: Interstitial lung diseases (ILD) associated with systemic autoimmune disease can have a strong negative impact on patient outcomes. The diagnostic gold standard is high-resolution computer tomography (HRCT). Numerous studies have proven lung ultrasound's (LUS) utility in ILD, as well as other lung pathologies. Recently, there has been more focus on ILD in rheumatoid arthritis (RA), a previously overlooked complication, and screening methods. The purpose of this systematic review was to summarize the recent knowledge regarding LUS compared to HRCT in screening ILD in RA patients. We reviewed relevant literature from the last 10 years and selected 10 articles. Results show that LUS is effective compared to HRCT as a screening tool. Several diagnostic and severity scores have been elaborated and tested. Further focus should be on LUS in long-term follow-up and standardization of protocols.
n8e712549147b: Sex and APOE {varepsilon}4 influence dementia risk, but whether its molecular predictors differ across sex and APOE {varepsilon}4 strata remains unclear. We investigated plasma proteomic and metabolomic signatures predicting future dementia in 43,759 UK Biobank participants across four sex-by-APOE {varepsilon}4 groups. The association between APOE {varepsilon}4 carrier status and dementia differed by sex (interaction p = 0.027). Machine-learning models achieved higher discrimination in APOE {varepsilon}4 carriers (AUC 0.85-0.90) than non-carriers (AUC 0.74-0.76), with the highest performance in female carriers. Most top molecular predictors were subgroup-specific, including C7, CDON and EDIL3 in female carriers and KLK4, MMP12 and TGFBI in male carriers. When UK Biobank models were applied to the Global Neurodegeneration Proteomics Consortium, 12/17 available top predictors in female carriers and 10/16 in male carriers remained highly ranked. These findings identify distinct molecular signatures of dementia risk across sex and APOE {varepsilon}4 strata, supporting stratified biomarker discovery.
nce753c9f7da3: Cancer among adolescents and young adults (AYAs) has been a growing public health concern in France since 2009, a priority reaffirmed in the new 2026-2030 roadmap of the Ten-Year Cancer Control Strategy. This issue is also generating increasing interest internationally, as evidenced by the emergence of scientific conferences dedicated to this population. However, the socioeconomic inequalities associated with cancer mortality among AYAs remain insufficiently documented internationally. The objective of this study is to analyze the socioeconomic determinants associated with cancer mortality among AYAs. Epidemiological data on cancer patients aged 15 to 39 are available for 37 countries for 2000 to 2023, these data being drawn from the Global Burden of Disease (GBD 2023) databases. For this study, they were supplemented by socioeconomic indicators from the United Nations Development Program and the World Bank. Descriptive analyses, correlations, principal component analysis, classification methods, time-series trend analyses (EAPC and Joinpoint), and panel data models have been performed. Results highlight a strong socioeconomic gradient in mortality. High-income countries have an average standardized mortality rate of 1.5 per 100,000 inhabitants, compared to 3.7 per 100,000 inhabitants in lower-middle-income countries. The mortality-to-incidence ratio decreases from 0.45 to 0.15 with increasing income level. Multivariate analyses confirm a significant association between the Human Development Index and cancer mortality among adolescents and young adults (AYAs), after adjusting for other model variables. Joinpoint analyses also reveal heterogeneous temporal trends according to sex and cancer type. This study highlights importance of socio-economic determinants in international inequalities in cancer mortality among AYAs.
nebbcf09c6b28: Background. African, Caribbean, and Black (ACB) communities in Canada experience a disproportionate burden of HIV, and a considerable share of infections among ACB immigrants is acquired after arrival in Canada. Yet how ACB people themselves understand the structural circumstances surrounding post-migration acquisition remains underexamined. This study asked how intersecting structural and social disadvantages shape post-migration HIV vulnerability among ACB communities in Ontario. Methods. We conducted an interpretive secondary thematic analysis of 44 in-depth interviews from the MSAFIRI Study, read through intersectionality and structural-vulnerability lenses. Interviews were coded inductively and deductively by two analysts, with consensus adjudication and community review of the thematic structure. Results. Five structural conditions organized participants accounts: racism as a structural condition of settlement; immigration precarity and the work of settling alone; economic precarity, including insecure work, poverty, and unstable housing; ruptured kin networks and isolation under migration; and gendered violence and homophobia. These conditions compounded one another, so that disadvantage in one domain deepened vulnerability in another. Conclusion. Post-migration HIV vulnerability among ACB communities is produced by intersecting structural disadvantages encountered in the receiving country context. Equitable HIV prevention requires structural and community-led responses that address immigration precarity, economic and housing insecurity, gendered violence, homophobia, and anti-Black racism, alongside biomedical and individual-level prevention. Keywords: HIV; African, Caribbean, and Black communities; migration; structural vulnerability; intersectionality; social determinants of health; Canada
n6da9346ff06d: Metformin use has been associated with a lower risk of incident dementia than other antidiabetics. We perform target trial emulation and causal competing risk analysis in the NIH All of Us (AoU) Research Program database, contrasting the effects of metformin and sulfonylurea initiation on dementia onset and death without dementia. AoU's social and behavioral health data allowed us to test robustness to excluding such confounders, and we further adjusted for calendar year effects and prior antidiabetic exposure, using both semiparametric Cox proportional hazards (PH) models and nonparametric models. Under stabilized inverse propensity score of treatment weighting, metformin was associated with a substantially lower risk of death (hazard ratio [HR]: 0.61, 95% CI: [0.49, 0.75]) and a lower incidence of dementia (HR: 0.90, 95% CI: [0.82, 1.02]). Estimated HRs were closely aligned with estimates obtained in the UK primary care and US Mass General Brigham health systems. This finding was robust to the inclusion of participants without a type 2 diabetes diagnosis at baseline and to the consideration of different covariate sets in the propensity score model, supporting metformin as a promising candidate for dementia prevention and motivating prospective validation.
nd8aa24e44552: Background In the UK, front-of-pack traffic light labels (TLL) are implemented voluntarily. The UK Government are considering alternative FOP approaches, such as nutrient warning labels (WL). However, the effects and potential harm of TLL versus WL in UK consumers are unclear. We compared the effects of WL, TLL, and no label on unhealthy food item selection and negative affect among UK adults with and without an eating disorder (ED). Methods We conducted two online randomised controlled trials. In Study 1, 924 UK adults without an ED diagnosis were randomly assigned (1:1:1) to a WL, TLL, or no labels condition and completed a food-choice task. In Study 2, 240 UK adults with an ED diagnosis completed a baseline no-label food choice task and were subsequently randomly assigned (1:1:1) to WL, TLL, or no labels for a follow-up food choice task. The primary outcome was the number of task-specific unhealthy food items selected. Negative affect before and after food choice tasks was measured as a secondary outcome. Findings In Study 1 (data collected 02/25 - 04/25), unhealthy food selection differed by condition (p = .013). Of five products selected, WL participants selected 0.20 fewer unhealthy items than TLL participants (8.0%; p = .038) and 0.28 fewer than controls (10.7%; p = .004). In Study 2 (data collected 11/25 - 02/26), unhealthy selection decreased by 0.39 items with WL (17.7%; p = .015), 0.13 with TLL (5.3%, p = .286), and 0.00 with no labels. The reduction was greater with WL than with no labels (p = .029). Label condition did not differentially affect task-related negative affect in either study (Study 1, p = .757; Study 2, p = .448). Interpretation WL tended to be associated with lower unhealthy food selection compared to TLL in UK adults. There was minimal evidence that WL or TLL caused negative emotional responses. Funding This research was funded by the National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) Oxford Health BRC. The views expressed are those of the author(s) and not necessarily those of the NIHR or the Department of Health and Social Care. Registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07339969
n98dfb7166f50: Background: About one-third of individuals with schizophrenia do not respond to first-line antipsychotics. Clozapine has superior efficacy for treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS), yet remains underutilised partly due to a 1% risk of potentially fatal clozapine-induced neutropenia (CIN). However, the biological mechanisms underlying CIN remain poorly understood. Methods: We recruited six individuals with TRS who had previously received clozapine: three who ceased clozapine following CIN and three who stopped for reasons unrelated to CIN. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were collected and cultured in vitro under three conditions: untreated, clozapine alone, or clozapine with its two major metabolites. Single nucleus RNA sequencing was performed to profile the cellular transcriptomic landscape following exposure to clozapine and its metabolites. Results: After quality control, 59,313 cells spanning 26 distinct clusters were retained. Multiple cell type-specific genes were differentially expressed in TRS with CIN, or in response to clozapine exposure in TRS donors with CIN (but not in those without CIN), after adjusting for age, sex and smoking status. We also identified a CIN-associated co-expression module in naive CD4 T cells that was driven by the transcription factor SREBF1, and robust evidence for differential cell-cell communication involving seven intercellular ligand-receptor pairs. There was limited evidence that clozapine-related metabolites contributed to these transcriptional changes. Conclusions: Our findings provide novel insights into cell type-specific transcriptional changes associated with CIN status and/or clozapine exposure in TRS with CIN. With replication in larger, independent cohorts, this work may contribute to the future development of predictive biomarkers for CIN and safer therapeutic strategies for TRS.
n5352c9bdd53c: Introduction: Supervision in psychological intervention training is limited by the time needed to evaluate simulated sessions. We tested a Vision Language Model (VLM) and Large Language Model (LLM) pipeline that assesses competency from verbal and nonverbal communication. Method: Gemini-3.1-Pro was used to annotate behaviors in 25 simulated therapy videos and incorporate them into transcripts, and ChatGPT-6.1-Sol rated them against the ENACT scale. Two clinicians verified VLM-identified behaviors and four independently rated each video. Agreement was estimated with Gwet's AC1 and ICC. Results: Of 1,558 VLM-identified behaviors, 70% were confirmed by both clinicians and 93% by at least one. AI-clinician agreement on therapeutic behavior attributes (AC1=0.73, 95% CI 0.70-0.76) approached between-clinician agreement (0.75, 0.72-0.78). AI-clinician ICCs on therapeutic domain levels (median 0.57) were modestly lower than between-clinician ICCs (0.67). Discussion: The pipeline agreed with clinicians nearly as well as clinicians agreed with each other and shows promise as a supplementary evaluator in therapist training.
nad38c3429544: Background & Objectives: As recently recommended by neuropathologists, we assessed the diagnostic accuracy of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) alpha-synuclein (-syn) seed amplification assay (SAA) in an autopsy cohort with systemic assessment of Lewy pathology. Methods: CSF was obtained antemortem and stored at -80 . -syn SAA and systemic Lewy pathology assessment were conducted as previously reported. Kinetic parameters, including maximum fluorescence (Fmax) and time to reach 50% of Fmax (T50), were also evaluated. Results: CSF samples were available from 30 patients (8 with symptomatic Lewy body disease [LBD], 2 with multiple system atrophy [MSA], 3 with Alzheimer's disease [AD], and 17 disease controls). Despite different clinical stages, all patients with LBD had diffuse neocortical or limbic-stage pathology at autopsy, with widespread peripheral Lewy bodies, including in the esophagus, heart, and sympathetic ganglia. Lewy pathology was not observed in disease controls. SAA was positive in all 8 with LBD, low positive in one patient with AD, and negative in all others. Fmax was significantly higher in LBD compared with cases without -syn pathology (9091{+/-}2083 vs. 1659{+/-}113 relative fluorescence units). The low-positive case had a lower positivity rate (25% vs. 75-100%), lower Fmax, and longer T50 than LBD cases. Conclusions: In this pilot study, CSF -syn SAA demonstrated high specificity (95%) and high sensitivity (100%) for detecting LBD; however, all LBD cases had widespread pathology, including peripheral involvement. Larger studies are needed to understand the association between CSF -syn SAA and Lewy pathology in the body.
ndd8f4ff5e2ae: Objective: Urban neighbourhoods across Europe are rapidly transforming through gentrification, with Portuguese cities particularly affected. Although the health impacts of these changes are increasingly recognised, validated instruments to assess perceptions of neighbourhood change remain scarce. This study adapted and validated a Portuguese version of the Perceptions About Change in Environment and Residents (PACER-PT) scale. Methods: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among 255 adults living for >=5yrs in the Lisbon and Porto Metropolitan Areas. PACER was translated and culturally adapted to create PACER-PT. We evaluated psychometric properties using exploratory factor analysis (EFA), internal consistency, and convergent and criterion validity. Results: EFA identified a three-factor structure explaining 47.5% of the variance: Built, social and economic changes, Positive attitude towards neighbourhood changes, and Displacement concerns and neighbourhood disruption. Internal consistency was acceptable (Cronbach s alpha=0.70-0.78). Convergent/criterion validity were supported by significant associations with amount and pace of change, self-rated health, and quality of life. Younger and wealthier participants and those with greater residential satisfaction reported more favourable perceptions. Conclusions: PACER-PT demonstrated it is a valid instrument for assessing gentrification-related neighbourhood changes in Portugal.
n612ec8a5560a: Purpose: This study, conducted by the Clinical Genome Resource Severe Combined Immunodeficiency Disease Variant Curation Expert Panel (ClinGen SCID-VCEP), aimed to adapt the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics/Association for Molecular Pathology (ACMG/AMP) framework for germline variant interpretation in RMRP. Unlike the protein-coding genes for which the framework was primarily developed, RMRP encodes a non-protein-coding RNA. Biallelic pathogenic variants in RMRP cause cartilage-hair hypoplasia, which can include severe combined immunodeficiency disease and other immune abnormalities. Methods: An RMRP-focused SCID-VCEP subgroup reviewed all 28 ACMG/AMP evidence criteria using population databases, published clinical and experimental data, computational predictions, and expert consensus. Each criterion was retained, modified, or designated as not applicable based on RMRP biology and disease mechanisms. The resulting specifications were pilot tested using 27 variants selected from ClinVar and research laboratory data. Results: Fifteen ACMG/AMP criteria were determined to be applicable to RMRP, while 13 were considered not applicable. Several criteria were modified to evaluate nucleotide-level effects on transcriptional regulation, critical promoter regions, and RNA secondary structure. The specifications also incorporated RMRP-specific recommendations for population frequency, functional evidence, variant phase, segregation, and phenotype. Application of the specifications classified 6 variants as pathogenic, 10 as likely pathogenic, 7 as variants of uncertain significance, and 4 as benign. Previously pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants remained within the pathogenic spectrum, and all previously benign variants remained benign. Variants with conflicting ClinVar interpretations were resolved as either likely pathogenic or uncertain. PM1, PM3, and PP4 were the primary criteria supporting pathogenic classifications. Conclusion: The SCID-VCEP specifications provide a standardized approach to the classification of germline RMRP variants in cartilage-hair hypoplasia and demonstrate how the ACMG/AMP framework can be adapted for a disease-associated non-protein-coding RNA gene. These specifications support the development of variant interpretation frameworks for other clinically relevant non-protein-coding genes.
nfbf04c0e916f: Matrix multiplication dominates both PHY signal processing and Deep Neural Network (DNN) inference, yet these domains place opposing demands on the matrix engine. Signal processing requires low-latency execution of relatively small matrix operations, whereas DNN inference, particularly at large batch sizes, prioritizes high throughput and energy efficiency for large matrix multiplications. While offering efficient memory access profile, a Systolic Array (SA) adds fill and drain delays per matrix. Those can be amortized for large matrices but not for small matrices. Conversely, a tensor unit completes the kernel in few cycles but would require repeated reads of same operand tiles over large matrices.
